title: Wedelolactone, a Novel TLR2 Agonist, Promotes Neutrophil Differentiation and Ameliorates Neutropenia: A Multi-Omics Approach to Unravel the Mechanism.
authors: Wang, Long; Li, Zhichao; Hu, Tianci; Li, Qinyao; Zhang, Linwei; Mei, Xinyue; Qi, Xiao; Liu, Sheng; Kong, Weijie; Luo, Jiesi; Wu, Anguo; Huang, Feihong; Li, Sirui; Dai, Shuang; Zhang, Chunxiang; Li, Rong; Wu, Jianming
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物WED通过TLR2-MEK/ERK通路促进中性粒细胞分化以缓解中性粒细胞减少症，虽涉及分子对接和转录因子表达，但核心是免疫药理而非蛋白质-DNA互作建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Neutropenia, a common complication in cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy, heightens the risk of infection and mortality, with limited treatment options. This study investigates wedelolactone (WED), a natural coumarin, as a potential therapeutic agent. WED is found to promote neutrophil differentiation and enhance bactericidal function in vitro. Its in vivo efficacy is validated in radiation-induced neutropenic mouse and zebrafish models, where it facilitates rapid recovery of leukocyte and neutrophil levels. An integrated approach using the GEO database, RNA sequencing, molecular docking, and Drug Affinity Responsive Target Stability (DARTS) assays identifies TLR2 and its downstream MAPK signaling pathway as essential for WED's anti-neutropenic effects. DARTS confirms significant binding of WED to TLR2. Knockdown of TLR2 with siRNA or inhibition of TLR2 with C29 reduces WED-induced neutrophil differentiation, MEK1/2 and ERK1/2 phosphorylation, and expression of transcription factors (PU.1, CEBPbeta). Similarly, ERK1/2 inhibition by SCH772984 impairs WED-induced neutrophil differentiation and bactericidal activity, decreasing PU.1 and CEBPbeta expression without affecting TLR2 levels. These findings position TLR2 as a key therapeutic target for neutropenia, with WED effectively promoting neutrophil differentiation via TLR2 and MEK/ERK pathway activation. This study highlights the therapeutic potential of targeting TLR2 to alleviate neutropenia and underscores the utility of a multi-omics approach in uncovering drug mechanisms.
abstract_zh: 中性粒细胞减少症是接受放疗的癌症患者中常见的并发症，会增加感染和死亡风险，且治疗选择有限。本研究探讨了天然香豆素类化合物蟛蜞菊内酯（wedelolactone, WED）作为潜在治疗药物的可能性。研究发现，WED在体外能促进中性粒细胞分化并增强杀菌功能。其体内疗效在辐射诱导的中性粒细胞减少小鼠和斑马鱼模型中得到验证，可促进白细胞和中性粒细胞水平的快速恢复。通过整合GEO数据库、RNA测序、分子对接和药物亲和力响应靶标稳定性（Drug Affinity Responsive Target Stability, DARTS）实验，确定TLR2及其下游MAPK信号通路是WED抗中性粒细胞减少作用的关键。DARTS实验证实WED与TLR2有显著结合。使用siRNA敲低TLR2或使用C29抑制TLR2，可降低WED诱导的中性粒细胞分化、MEK1/2和ERK1/2磷酸化，以及转录因子（PU.1、CEBPbeta）的表达。同样，SCH772984抑制ERK1/2会损害WED诱导的中性粒细胞分化和杀菌活性，降低PU.1和CEBPbeta表达，但不影响TLR2水平。这些发现将TLR2定位为中性粒细胞减少症的关键治疗靶点，WED通过激活TLR2和MEK/ERK通路有效促进中性粒细胞分化。本研究凸显了靶向TLR2缓解中性粒细胞减少症的治疗潜力，并强调了多组学方法在揭示药物机制中的价值。
